No. 001 · Atlanta

Absinthe Frappe

Total Entries

1

Origin: Atlanta — Empire State South — ESS • LIQUEURS, APERITIFS & FORTIFIED WINE

Cocktail Ingredients:

  • 1 oz Absinthe
  • 0.5 oz Water
  • 1 bar spoon to 0.5 oz Simple Syrup

Technique:

Shake with ice, strain, top with soda.

Glassware & Garnish:

Served in Rocks Glass / Crushed Ice and garnished with mint leaf.

House Made Ingredients:

None — no house-made ingredient in this build.

Spirit Descriptions & Substitutions:

Absinthe — anise-forward, herbal, and potent. Substitution: use another quality absinthe; pastis is the closest, with a softer profile.

— Behind Bar —

Afternoon Howdy

Total Entries

1

Technique:

Stir no less than 18 seconds.

Glassware & Garnish:

House Made Ingredients:

Spirit Descriptions & Substitutions:

Rum — cane spirit ranging from light and grassy to dark and molasses-rich. Substitution: match the style — white rum for light and clean, aged rum for depth and caramel. No. 003 · Atlanta

Alpine Summer

Total Entries

1

Origin: Atlanta — Empire State South — ESS • GIN

Cocktail Ingredients:

  • 1 oz Hayman's Royal Dock Gin
  • 0.75 oz Dolin Genepi
  • 0.75 oz Cocchi Rosa
  • 0.75 oz Lemon Juice
  • 0.25 oz Violette Liqueur
  • 1 dash Swedish Herb Bitters
  • Top with Prosecco

Technique:

Shake, Fine Strain up, top with prosecco.

Glassware & Garnish:

Served in Leopold Coupe.

House Made Ingredients:

None — no house-made ingredient in this build.

Spirit Descriptions & Substitutions:

Gin — juniper-forward with botanicals, citrus, and spice. London Dry is classic and crisp. Substitution: use a London Dry gin for the classic profile; for a softer build, try a contemporary gin with citrus and floral notes. Vermouth — aromatized, fortified wine with herbs and botanicals. Substitution: use a fresh, quality vermouth in the same style (sweet, dry, or blanc) and keep it refrigerated after opening. Wine — in this build it brings acidity and fruit. Substitution: use a fresh, dry wine in the same style; sparkling wine should be fresh and well-chilled.

House Made Ingredients:

Recipe Name: Milk Punch Ingredients List: 10 oz Bombay Sapphire 6 oz Pear Brandy 2 oz Banana Liquor 1 oz Angostura Bitters 2 oz Almon Tincture 16 oz French vanilla Tea 8 oz Hot Water 12 oz Citrus (lime/lemon) 1 quart sugar 3 Bananas 2 Ginger Nubs 3 Cinnamon Sticks 6 Star Anise 3 Nutmeg Coriander Seed Chinchona Bark Prep Instructions: Combine ingredients per the original method.

Recipe Name: Milk Punch Recipe Ingredients List: First peel lime & lemons ( 8 eight of them) chop the bananas and ginger, peel skins and loosely cut into Prep Instructions: Chunks. Add a quart of sugar to a large container - this will extract the oil from the citrus peels. toss the banana's and ginger's into the sugar, along with the lime and lemos peels and the juice of 12 citrus. Toast cinnamon's sticks, cloves, coriander, star anise and nutmeg add to the mix. Stir up the mixture so that fruit, spices and sugar are combined creating a oleo saccharum. From here, add of the spirits and hot tea before allowing the combination to macerate for 24 hours.after adding your spirits, stir everything to combine now, brew eight ounces of french vanilla tea and the hot tea to the mixture, along with 16 ounces of hot water. From here, quickly cover the container and allow it to macerate for 24 hours. After allowing the combination to sit for 24 hours, strain out the solids, gently pressing the mash through a sieve to get banana's juices. Now, add a half gallon of milk and half quart of almonds and tincture, once boiled, carefully pour the almond milk into a separate container with 10 oz of lemons juice. The lemon juice will begin the process of curdling, which will separate the milk's liquid and solids. Combine the punch mixture with the almond milk mixture. From here allow the combination to sit for two hours so it can come down to room temperature. Once that's happened, strain the large curds out by pouring the mixture through a sieve. Leave the liquid in a cool, dark place ( or refrigerate) overnight so it can separate. After separation occurs, use a large ladle to scoop of the top and run the mix through a superbag or coffe filter to clarified.

Recipe Name: Blue Bubbles Ingredients List: 10 oz Soda Water 10 oz tonic Syrup 2 oz Lime Juice 1.5 oz Lecithin 2 drops blue food color Prep Instructions: Combine ingredients and stir well to combine. Using hand blender froth the mixture to create a light foam.

Recipe Name: Lime Oleo Sacchrum Ingredients List: 1 day worth of lime discards from juicing. 7 quarts sugar 4 quarts water 1 Quart of citric acid Prep Instructions: Take a day's worth of lime discards that Pierline will save for us. Cover evenly with 6 quarts of sugar and beat the crap out of it with long spoons and/or muddlers. Let sit for one full day. Stir oils and peels around to saturate and break down the sugar. Boil 4 quarts of water, add to lime oleo, add one quart sugar, stir until all is dissolved. Fine strain so there is not pulp left in the lime syrup. Add at a quarter quart at a time citric acid to taste. The first time I made the syrup I used nearly an entire quart of citric acid to the 12 quart batch of lime oleo.

Spirit Descriptions & Substitutions:

Mezcal — a smoky agave spirit from Oaxaca, earthy and complex with notes of smoke, citrus, and roasted agave. Substitution: use another quality mezcal in the same style; for less smoke, split with a blanco tequila, or use a reposado tequila with a whisper of peated whisky. Vodka — a clean, neutral spirit that lets the modifiers shine. Substitution: any quality unflavored vodka works; a wheat or potato vodka adds a touch more body. Vermouth — aromatized, fortified wine with herbs and botanicals. Substitution: use a fresh, quality vermouth in the same style (sweet, dry, or blanc) and keep it refrigerated after opening.
